judgments.evidence: src/model.jl:129-132: Model(build, T; chunk_size, kw...) = Model(Deployment(build; kw...), T; chunk_size), and Model(root, T; kw...) = Model(build(root), T; kw...), so the deployment (and the build) are evaluated before the scalar check at src/model.jl:111. Probe P3 results. Model(build, Float32; Δt_frame=-1) gives DeploymentInvalid :range on Δt_frame. Model(build, Float32) gives DeploymentInvalid :missing on Δt_frame. Model(root, Float32; Δt_frame=-1) gives DeploymentInvalid. A root that fails to build, at Float32, gives PathResolution + UnconnectedInput. Model(dep, Float32; chunk_size=0) gives :scalar alone, so the claim holds for the deployment form only.
judgments.fix: Appendix C: '`Model(deployment, T)` at a scalar other than `Float64` or a concrete `ForwardDiff.Dual` over `Float64`, nested or not, raises it with reason `:scalar`, alone and before its keywords are read ([D-320]). The composed forms build the deployment first, so its refusals come ahead of the scalar's.' Docstring: '... is refused as `ArgumentInvalid` with reason `:scalar`, before the model compiles anything. `Model(build; kw...)` and `Model(root; kw...)` build the deployment first, and its refusals come first.'
judgments.backing_entry: D-320 backs the scalar check on `Model(deployment, T)` only. D-254 (the composed forms defined as the composition) backs the code's order. The alternative is a code change that checks T first in the composed forms, so the fix is a choice.
judgments.note: For the root form, build(root) runs the whole build pipeline, including the nominal Float64 activation, before the refusal. So the docstring's 'before anything is compiled' is also too broad there.

src/structure.jl:139-198 defines the row types and `membership`. Probe P7: Structure's fields are Vector{ComponentEntry}, Vector{Anchor}, Vector{RateScope NamedTuple}, Vector{Symbol}, Vector{Type} and Vector{LevelEntry}. The module exports nothing (src/Redstone.jl has no export, per D-226), and docstring_rules.md rule 1 takes docs/src/api.md as the public set. api.md lists `Structure` but none of its row types, so they are internal. Spec §9.1 (design/spec.md:4958-4976) states the facts the rows hold: the components by path with their tier and rate chain, and one row per assembly with its children (each with its contributing field) and its wires. It does so without naming the types.
judgments.note: The statement is accurate as a fact: spec, Appendix B and api.md name no row type. But nothing in the docs contradicts the code, and the row type names are internal. D-261 in the log names ComponentEntry and Anchor. Whether Structure's fields and row types become public is owed to the exported-name audit (design/pending.md:89-96, 'It also settles which fields are public'). If they are made public, this becomes a gap row for that bullet.
